Today is very special day for me. I wake up early because I am so nervous, my hand even shaking a little when I eat breakfast. My husband tell me "you will be fine" but I still worry so much, maybe too much. The test center was not far, only twenty minute by bus, but I arrive one hour early anyway because I am always like this when something important happening.

The instructor was older man, very quiet, he did not smile much which make me more nervous. We drive around the city for maybe thirty minute, he ask me to do the parallel parking two time, first one was not so good but second one I think was okay. Also he ask me to drive on the highway little bit, that part I was scare of but I think I do fine.

When we come back to the center he write something on his paper for long time and I could not breathe properly, just waiting. Then finally he look at me and say "congratulations, you pass." I almost cry right there in the car! I text my husband immediately, he say he is so proud of me. Tonight we will celebrate with dinner at the Italian place we like. state:
Quick update for anyone following the community garden proposal on the old lot at the end of Poplar Street. I finally got a callback from the city planning office after three weeks of leaving messages, which honestly felt like its own achievement. Here's where things stand.

The lot is currently zoned for light commercial use, so before anything can happen we need a variance, which means a public hearing. I've already submitted the paperwork and the earliest slot they had was the second Tuesday of next month, so that's now on the calendar. In the meantime, the planning office confirmed the soil testing from two years ago is still on file and apparently still valid, which saves us the cost of retesting, a nice bit of good news.

On the design side, I sketched out a rough layout with twelve raised beds, a small tool shed near the fence line, and a rainwater collection barrel by the shed. I based the bed spacing loosely on the community garden two neighborhoods over, since a few of us visited it last month and it seemed to work well for accessibility, wide enough paths for wheelchairs and that sort of thing.

Funding-wise, we've got about 40% of what we'd need from the neighborhood association's discretionary fund, and I'm looking into a few small grants aimed at urban greening projects. If anyone has grant-writing experience and a free evening sometime, I would very much welcome the help. I'll post again after the hearing with whatever they decide.

state: This lentil soup has become our Sunday standby, and here's exactly how I make it now after several rounds of tweaking. Rinse two cups of brown lentils, then sauté one diced onion, two carrots, and two celery stalks in two tablespoons of olive oil until soft, about eight minutes. Add three cloves of minced garlic, one tablespoon of cumin, one teaspoon of smoked paprika, and a bay leaf, stir for thirty seconds, then pour in six cups of vegetable stock along with the lentils. Simmer uncovered for thirty-five to forty minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender but not mushy, then finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of good olive oil right before serving. If it thickens too much overnight, just thin it with a splash of stock when reheating.
